announcements.title: Important Guidelines for Paper 4 – Review Paper and Presentation
announcements.body:
Dear Students,

For those preparing a Review Paper for Paper 4, please pay attention to the following points when preparing your final paper and PowerPoint presentation.

1. Review Methodology Section

Your Review Methodology should clearly explain:

- Search Sources: Which databases you used to find relevant papers.

- Search Keywords: Which keywords or search terms you used.

- Selection Criteria: How you decided which papers to include or exclude.

- Selection Process: How many papers you found, screened, excluded, and finally selected.

- Data Extraction: What information you collected from each paper.

- Literature Synthesis: How you organized, compared, and analyzed the selected studies.
Describe what you actually did. Do not invent search results or selection numbers. If you use the term Systematic Review , your methodology must clearly support that description.

2. PowerPoint Presentation

Please make sure your presentation:

- Includes a slide explaining your review methodology and paper selection process.

- Clearly presents the research problem and research questions/objectives.

- Compares the selected studies instead of only summarizing them individually.

- Uses clear tables or figures to highlight important findings.

- Explains how the findings address your research questions.

- Includes the main conclusions, limitations, and future work.

- Provides appropriate citations and references.
Remember: The main objective of Paper 4 is to demonstrate your understanding of how to structure and write a research paper. Focus on clarity, organization, proper referencing, and meaningful discussion of the findings.

Best regards,

Prof. Mohammed Alwakeel

announcements.title: Important Notice Regarding Grade Distribution and Research Submission Quality
announcements.body:
Dear Students,

As stated in the official course specification shared with you on Blackboard at the beginning of the semester , the grade distribution for CSC 608 – Research Methods is as follows:

Grade Distribution:

- Paper 1: 15 marks (Published Research Paper, Written Report, and PowerPoint Presentation).

- Paper 2: 15 marks (Published Research Paper, Written Report, and PowerPoint Presentation).

- Paper 3: 15 marks (Published Research Paper, Written Report, and PowerPoint Presentation).

- Paper 4 – Final Research Paper: 30 marks.

- Paper 4 – PowerPoint Presentation: 15 marks.

- Class Participation Throughout the Semester: 10 marks.
Total: 100 marks.

Important Reminder Regarding Submission Quality and Academic Expectations

I strongly urge all students to take these assessment requirements seriously and make every effort to avoid losing marks unnecessarily.

After reviewing some of the submissions received for Paper 1, I noticed that a small number of students submitted work that clearly indicates they had not carefully read or followed the research guidelines document and the previous email instructions.

The quality, completeness, and academic standard of these submissions fall significantly below what is expected and required at the master's level .

Please understand that failure to follow the specified instructions, incomplete submissions, and work that does not meet the required academic standards will directly affect the marks awarded for the corresponding assessment.

I would therefore like to emphasize that every student is expected to carefully read and follow the CSC608_Student_Research_Work_Guidelines.pdf document, along with all previous announcements and instructions sent through Blackboard.

Your written reports must demonstrate a genuine understanding and critical evaluation of the selected research papers. Simply copying information or providing a superficial summary is not sufficient. Likewise, your presentations must be complete, well-organized, and academically appropriate.

Submitting the required files does not automatically entitle a student to full marks. The marks awarded will depend on the quality, completeness, academic content, and compliance with the specified requirements.

I also remind you that 10 marks are allocated to class participation throughout the semester , and students are expected to participate actively and be prepared to discuss their research work when requested.

I strongly encourage everyone to review the guidelines and previous instructions carefully before making any further submissions. Please take the necessary steps to improve the quality of your work and avoid losing marks that could otherwise be earned.

I expect all students to demonstrate the level of academic effort, critical thinking, and professionalism appropriate for a master's degree program.

Best regards,

Prof. Mohammed Alwakeel

announcements.title: Important Instructions for All Future Submissions (ZIP Files and Required Formats)
announcements.body:
Dear Students,

IMPORTANT: Please read this entire message carefully and make sure you fully understand and follow all the instructions below.

First, I would like to confirm that the files you have already submitted have been received. There is no need to resend any previously submitted files. The following instructions apply only to new submissions from now on .

However, I have noticed some issues with the formats and organization of previously submitted files. To avoid these problems in future submissions, all students must strictly follow the requirements below.

1. Mandatory ZIP File for All Future Submissions

Effective immediately, whenever you submit multiple files through Blackboard Messages, you must:

- Place ALL required files into ONE compressed ZIP (.zip) file .

- Send only ONE ZIP file as an attachment to your Blackboard message.

- Do NOT send files as separate attachments or in multiple messages.

- Before sending, verify that the ZIP file opens correctly, is not corrupted, and contains all the required files.

- Do NOT password-protect or encrypt the ZIP file. It must be accessible without requiring any password.

- Make sure that all files inside the ZIP archive are complete, correctly named, and in the required formats.
These instructions are mandatory for all future submissions and must be followed without exception.

2. Required File Formats – Important Clarification

Please carefully reread the previous announcement regarding the research work requirements for Weeks 11–15.

I have noticed that some students submitted only Word documents without the required PDF versions. Others submitted only PowerPoint presentations without including the PDF versions of the same presentations.

To avoid any further confusion, the required file formats are as follows:

- Written Reports and Research Papers: PDF (.pdf) only.

- Presentations: Each presentation must be submitted in TWO separate formats :

- PowerPoint (.pptx).

- PDF (.pdf) version of the same presentation.

- Selected Published Journal Articles (Papers 1–3): PDF (.pdf) only.
IMPORTANT: Submitting a PowerPoint file without its corresponding PDF version is incomplete. Likewise, submitting a Word document instead of the required PDF does not meet the submission requirements.

All required files must be included in the same ZIP archive.

3. Submission Through Blackboard Messages

All future submissions must follow these steps:

- Prepare all the required files in the correct formats.

- Place all files into ONE ZIP archive .

- Verify that the ZIP file opens correctly, contains all required files, and is not password-protected.

- Send the ZIP file to me as an attachment using the Messages feature in Blackboard , not the Assignment Submission feature.

- IMPORTANT: Make sure to check the “Send an email copy to recipients” option before sending your message. This step is mandatory.

- Complete your submission before the deadline specified for the corresponding week.
4. Student Responsibility and Compliance

Each student is personally responsible for:

- Carefully reading and following the previous announcement and the instructions in this email.

- Submitting ALL required files , not just some of them.

- Ensuring that every file is provided in the correct format.

- Checking that the ZIP archive is complete, accessible, and free from errors.

- Ensuring that the ZIP file is not password-protected.

- Following the correct Blackboard Messages submission procedure.

- Meeting the announced submission deadlines.
Incomplete submissions, missing files, incorrect file formats, corrupted ZIP archives, or password-protected ZIP files will not be considered valid reasons for extending submission deadlines.

5. Important Reminder Regarding Previous Submissions

To avoid any misunderstanding:

- All files previously sent have been received.

- You do NOT need to resend any files that you have already submitted.

- The new ZIP file requirement applies ONLY to future submissions.

- The purpose of this announcement is to ensure that all upcoming submissions are complete, properly formatted, and correctly organized.
Please take these instructions seriously and ensure full compliance with all requirements for future submissions.

Thank you for your cooperation.

Best regards,

Prof. Mohammed Alwakeel

announcements.title: Research Submissions, Deadlines, and Class Requirements (Weeks 11–15)
announcements.body:
Dear Students

As outlined in the CSC608_Student_Research_Work_Guidelines.pdf document available on Blackboard, please carefully review the following requirements, submission deadlines, and planned class activities from Week 11 (Current Week) through Week 15.

Week 11 (Current Week) – Paper 1

Each student must submit the following for Paper 1:

1.  Written Report (PDF).

2.  Presentation (both PowerPoint and PDF formats).

3.  PDF copy of the selected published journal paper.

Submission Deadline: Monday of Week 11 (Current Week), no later than 10:00 PM.

During the class in Week 11 (Current Week), selected students will be asked to present and discuss their submitted work. All students must be prepared to explain their papers and answer questions.

Week 12 (Next Week) – Papers 2 and 3

Each student must submit the following for each of Paper 2 and Paper 3 :

1.  Written Report (PDF).

2.  Presentation (both PowerPoint and PDF formats).

3.  PDF copy of the selected published journal paper.

Submission Deadline: Monday of Week 12, no later than 10:00 PM.

During the Week 12 class, selected students will be asked to present and discuss their submitted work. All students must be prepared to explain and answer questions about both papers.

Week 13 – Paper 4 Discussion and Guidance

The Week 13 class will be dedicated to discussing any questions, concerns, or points requiring clarification to help students complete the preparation of Paper 4 (Your Own Research Paper).

Each student should come prepared with any questions related to their research topic, research problem, objectives, methodology, literature review, paper structure, or other aspects of Paper 4.

No formal submission is required for Week 13.

Week 14 – Paper 4 Draft Submission

Each student must submit:

1.  Draft Research Paper (PDF).

2.  Draft Presentation (both PowerPoint and PDF formats).

Submission Deadline: Monday of Week 14, no later than 10:00 PM.

During the Week 14 class, selected research paper drafts will be presented and discussed. Feedback will focus on the research problem, objectives, literature review, methodology, findings, discussion, and overall quality of the research paper.

Week 15 – Paper 4 Final Submission

Each student must submit:

1.  Final Research Paper (PDF).

2.  Final Presentation (both PowerPoint and PDF formats).

Submission Deadline: Monday of Week 15, no later than 10:00 PM.

During the Week 15 class, selected students will be asked to present and discuss their final research papers. All students must be prepared to explain and defend their work.

Important Submission and USB Flash Drive Requirements

Please pay careful attention to the following mandatory requirements:

1. Submission via Blackboard Email

·     All required files must be sent directly to me as email attachments through the Blackboard email system by the specified deadline for the corresponding week.

·     Do not upload your files through the Blackboard Assignment Submission feature. All required files must be sent directly to me as attachments using the Messages feature in Blackboard. IMPORTANT: When sending your message, make sure to check the “Send an email copy to recipients” option. This step is mandatory and must not be overlooked.

·     All written reports, research papers, and copies of published journal articles must be submitted in PDF format.

·     All presentations must be submitted in both PowerPoint (.pptx) and PDF (.pdf) formats.

·     Students are responsible for ensuring that all required files are correctly attached to their emails before sending.

·     Late submissions will not be accepted.

2. Mandatory USB Flash Drive for Class

In addition to sending the required files by email through Blackboard, every student must bring a USB flash drive containing all the required files for the corresponding week to that week’s scheduled class session (Week 11 (Current Week), Week 12, Week 14, and Week 15).

·     The USB flash drive must contain copies of all files required for that week’s submission.

·     All written reports, research papers, and published articles must be available in PDF format.

·     All presentation files must be available in both PowerPoint and PDF formats.

·     Students must be ready to transfer their files from the USB flash drive to my computer and present their work during class if requested.

·     All files must be properly organized, accessible, and ready for immediate use during the class.

·     This requirement applies to every student, regardless of whether they are selected to present.

3. General Requirements

·     Sending the required files by email through Blackboard and bringing the same files on a USB flash drive are two separate mandatory requirements. Completing one does not replace the other.

·     Every student is responsible for ensuring that all required files are complete, correctly formatted, and submitted on time.

·     All students must be prepared to present and discuss their work, even if they are not selected to do so.

·     All work must comply with the requirements specified in the guidelines document available on Blackboard.

Important: All submissions must be sent to me by email through Blackboard, and the required files must also be brought on a USB flash drive to the corresponding class session.

Please plan your work carefully, meet all deadlines, and come fully prepared for each class.

Best regards,

Mohammed Alwakeel

University of Tabuk
